governing_owner_decisions.applies_as: the full pre-registered parity campaign must be run before a kernel remains ADMITTED; the reference it is scored against changed, so the v1 verdicts no longer bind the current tree
whatever the v2 verdicts, the default backend stays 'python'; frozen datasets, golden/reference rebuilds and score-bearing evidence are produced or independently reproduced by the Python reference
the reason for this re-registration: the canonical Python reference abep_sim/intake_tpmc.py was changed by these decisions (see reason_for_v2)

registration_statement: Written and committed in its own commit before any v2 Python-vs-Rust comparison was executed against the changed reference. At the time of this commit no v2 campaign, development comparison or recompute had been run against abep_sim/intake_tpmc.py at the sha256 pinned below, and the abep_core extension had not been rebuilt for v2. Every tolerance, observable, vector set, seed, sample size and decision rule below is copied unchanged from v1 (cited by sha256) and fixed for v2; none may be changed after the first v2 scoring campaign. Any change requires parity_prereg_v3; every v1 and v2 campaign stays on record.

supersedes.v1_status_after_v2: immutable history: the v1 pre-registration and report are never edited or rewritten; their verdicts stand only for the v1 reference sha256 (ea0100b9...) and the v1 build provenance, and no longer bind the current tree

reason_for_v2.bit_identity_evidence_from_step_2: docs/HISTORY.md entry '2026-10-01 — A9.9 S2.5 (F9-OQ-04): MCC-05/06/07 intake_tpmc input validation' and commit 153c013: valid-input numerics of trace_channel and intake_response (Maxwell and CLL) were checked bit-identical against the pre-change module. This is step-2 evidence about the reference only; it admits nothing here. The v2 campaign re-scores every kernel in full against the changed reference (A9.14 S10.4).
reason_for_v2.rust_sources: abep_core/ sources are unchanged since v1 (sha256 identical to the v1 build_provenance.source_sha256 for Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, pyproject.toml, src/lib.rs, src/rng.rs, src/tpmc.rs); the extension is rebuilt from them for v2 and its sha256 is recorded in the v2 report

reference_implementation.rule: the campaign refuses to score (status REFUSED_REFERENCE_CHANGED) if the reference file sha256 differs from sha256_at_registration; a changed reference needs a new pre-registration (v3)

what_this_is_not: not physics evidence: parity with the Python reference shows only that the Rust code reproduces abep_sim/intake_tpmc.py in distribution; it says nothing about whether the TPMC model is right
not a validation of the intake, of the frozen intake surface or of any design

not authority: no Rust result becomes authoritative because it is faster or because it is ADMITTED (A9.7); the Python reference stays authoritative, the frozen intake_surface_v1 data and goldens are never rebuilt with Rust
not a performance requirement: the measured speed-up is reported, it does not decide admission

kernels.algorithm_to_reproduce: draw 3n drifting-Maxwellian velocities (component sd sqrt(k_B T/m), drift V cos(theta) on z, V sin(theta) on x), keep v_z > 0, resample n with replacement with probability proportional to v_z
v_n = vth sqrt(-2 ln U), U ~ U[1e-12, 1); two tangential N(0, vth); tangent basis t1 = normal x z (normal x x when |t1| < 1e-9), normalised; t2 = normal x t1

Lord 1991 sampling exactly as coded: v_t,out = sqrt(1-alpha_t) v_t + sqrt(alpha_t) N3(0, v_mp/sqrt 2), normal component projected out; r = sqrt(-alpha_n ln U), th = 2 pi U, vm = sqrt(1-alpha_n)|v_n|/v_mp, v_n,out = v_mp sqrt(r^2 + vm^2 + 2 r vm cos th)

uniform entry position on the disc (r = R sqrt U, phi = 2 pi U), ballistic flight to wall / back plane z = L / front plane z = 0 with the same tie rules (exit_back if t_back <= t_wall and t_back <= t_front; exit_front if t_front < t_wall and t_front < t_back), Maxwell (diffuse with probability alpha, else specular) or CLL (alpha_n, alpha_t default alpha) wall kernel, hit budget max_hits doubled up to max_hits_cap while unresolved fraction > unresolved_tol; unresolved molecules reported, never assigned
diffuse entry about +z at T_w, Maxwell trace (scattering default), returns collected fraction

random_streams.statement: numpy and Rust random streams differ by construction. Parity is statistical, plus exact invariants. The Rust generator is xoshiro256++ (Blackman and Vigna) seeded through SplitMix64 from one 64-bit seed; normal deviates by the Marsaglia polar method; uniform doubles on [0,1) from the top 53 bits. Implemented in abep_core without external RNG crates so that the stream does not depend on crate versions.
random_streams.wrapper_seeding: abep_sim/design/tpmc_backend.py derives the Rust seed from one draw of the caller's numpy Generator: int(rng.integers(0, 2**64, dtype=numpy.uint64)). The same Generator state therefore gives the same Rust output (deterministic seeding).

campaign_seeds.derivation: vector k (0-based, in the registered order of its kernel) of kernel index j (K1=1 .. K5=5) uses numpy.random.default_rng(numpy.random.SeedSequence([master, j, k, s])) with s = 0 for the Python-backend generator, s = 1 for the generator from which the Rust seed is drawn, s = 2 for shared inputs (v0 for K4, v_in / normals for K2 and K3), s = 3 for the randomized-domain draws (k = 0 for the whole draw). K1 replicate r uses s = 10 + 2 r (Python) and s = 11 + 2 r (Rust).
campaign_seeds.development_rule: development and debugging comparisons use development_master_seed only and are never scored or reported as a verdict. Every execution of the scoring campaign is appended to the report's campaign history; no execution may be discarded.

golden_vectors.source: abep_sim/data/intake_surface_v1.json grid (frozen), cross-checked against the unique values in intake_surface_v1.csv
golden_vectors.conditions: atmosphere(200.0, 'mean') from the frozen NRLMSIS dataset (V, T); T_w = 350 K and d = 10 mm (IntakeGeometry defaults used to build the frozen surface); CLL with alpha_n = alpha_t = alpha (intake_response passes neither)
golden_vectors.phi_note: phi enters only the intake_response bookkeeping, never trace_channel; the 2 phi values are therefore one trace vector each (recorded as covered, not traced twice)
golden_vectors.K4_vectors: 4 L/d x 5 alpha x 3 theta x 3 species x 2 scattering = 360, n = 8000 particles each, v0 from the Python entry kernel (shared by both backends)
golden_vectors.K5_vectors: 4 L/d x 5 alpha x 3 species = 60 (Maxwell, as clausing_transmission calls trace_channel), n = 20000 each (the value intake_response uses)
golden_vectors.K2_vectors: 3 species x 2 normal sets (+z wall normal; random unit normals in the x-y plane as on the channel wall) = 6, T_w = 350 K, n = 20000
golden_vectors.K3_vectors: 3 species x 9 (alpha_n, alpha_t) pairs {(0,0),(1,1),(0,1),(1,0),(0.2,0.2),(0.5,0.5),(0.8,0.8),(0.3,0.9),(0.9,0.3)} = 27, T_w = 350 K, n = 20000; v_in = Python-entry velocities at 200 km mean, theta 5 deg, random x-y wall normals, normal component sign forced into the wall

K4.note: long channel: exercises the budget doubling

edge_cases.K4_defaults: species N2, atmosphere(200.0, 'mean'), T_w 350 K, d 10 mm, max_hits 200, max_hits_cap 5000, unresolved_tol 1e-3, n = 4000
edge_cases.K5_defaults: species N2, T_w 350 K, d 10 mm, n = 20000
edge_cases.K2_defaults: species N2, n = 20000; minus_z and plus_z exercise the fallback tangent basis (normal parallel to z)

randomized_domain.draw: one numpy Generator per kernel (s = 3). K4: L/d log-uniform on [0.5, 30]; scattering maxwell or cll with probability 1/2; maxwell alpha ~ U[0,1]; cll alpha_n, alpha_t ~ U[0,1] independently; theta ~ U[0, 15] deg; species uniformly from (O, N2, O2, mean molecular mass); altitude from (180, 200, 230) km and solar from (low, mean, high), frozen atmosphere; T_w ~ U[250, 450] K; d = 10 mm; n = 8000. K5: L/d log-uniform [0.5, 30], alpha ~ U[0,1], species as K4, T_w ~ U[250, 450] K, n = 20000. K1: theta ~ U[0, 15] deg, species, altitude and solar as K4. K2: T_w ~ U[250, 450] K, species as K4, normal set x_y_wall, n = 20000. K3: alpha_n, alpha_t ~ U[0,1], T_w ~ U[250, 450] K, species as K4, n = 20000. Draws are made in exactly this field order per vector.
randomized_domain.domain_note: numerical parity domain only; the ranges are not physics, design or evidence claims

K1_entry.se_method: replicate: each backend's value is the mean over its 32 replicate means; se = sample sd of the replicate means / sqrt(32). Replicates are used because the reference resamples with replacement from a finite pool, so particle-level se would be optimistic.

K3_cll.definitions: vn_out = v_out . normal; vt_out2 = |v_out|^2 - vn_out^2; vt_retention = (v_out,t . v_in,t) / |v_in,t|^2 per particle (0 when |v_in,t| = 0)

K4_trace.definitions: f_trans = collected fraction (transmission); f_back = backscatter fraction; f_unres = returned unresolved fraction (lost); mean_hits, mean_hits2 = mean of wall hits and of their square; mean_vz_trans, mean_v2_trans = mean v_z and |v|^2 of the final velocity over collected molecules; mean_vz_back, mean_v2_back = the same over backscattered molecules; mean_dpz = mean over all molecules of (v0_z - [back] v_out_z), the per-unit-mass momentum transfer intake_response uses for C_D
K4_trace.se_method: particle-level, conditional on the shared v0: given identical inputs the molecules are independent in both backends, so se = sd / sqrt(n_subset) is valid; because the sd also contains the spread of v0 across molecules it over-estimates the conditional se (conservative)

decision_rules.per_test: for every kernel, vector and observable: |mean_rust - mean_py| <= z * sqrt(se_py^2 + se_rust^2) with z = 5.0
decision_rules.z_basis: about 5,000 registered tests; two-sided normal tail at z = 5 is 5.7e-7, so the expected number of false rejections over the campaign is about 0.003 (K1 uses replicate se with 31 degrees of freedom per side; its tail at 5 is below 1e-5, about 2e-3 expected false rejections over its 150 tests)
decision_rules.zero_se_rule: if se_py = se_rust = 0 the observable is deterministic under both backends and must agree to |diff| <= 1e-12 * max(1, |mean_py|)
decision_rules.not_scored_rule: a conditional observable (K4 *_trans, *_back) is NOT_SCORED for a vector when either backend has fewer than conditional_min_count molecules in the subset; NOT_SCORED is reported, never counted as agreement
decision_rules.aggregate_bias: per kernel and observable, over all scored vectors with nonzero combined se: |sum_i z_i| / sqrt(N) <= 4.0, z_i = (mean_rust - mean_py) / sqrt(se_py^2 + se_rust^2); detects a systematic bias too small for any single vector
decision_rules.kernel_verdict: ADMITTED iff every exact invariant of the kernel holds in BOTH backends, every scored per-test check holds, every aggregate check holds, and the Rust build provenance is recorded; otherwise NOT_ADMITTED. An invariant that the Python reference itself violates is reported as REFERENCE_INVARIANT_FINDING and the kernel is NOT_ADMITTED (no Rust kernel is admitted against a reference behaviour the campaign could not confirm).
decision_rules.meaning_of_ADMITTED: the kernel may be selected explicitly (backend='rust') as an optional, switchable acceleration of the TPMC trace inside the tested parity domain. It is never the default, never silently substituted, never used to rebuild frozen data or goldens, and never authoritative; the Python reference reproduces every result.
decision_rules.no_retuning: z, the aggregate threshold, the observables, the vectors, n and the seeds are fixed. A NOT_ADMITTED verdict can be followed only by a code fix plus parity_prereg_v2 with a new scoring_master_seed; the v1 record stays.

exact_invariants.statement: partition: every molecule is exactly one of collected, backscattered or unresolved (never both collected and back); counts sum to n; the returned unresolved fraction equals the unresolved count / n
I/O shapes and types: collected bool (n,), v float64 (n,3), hits integer (n,), back bool (n,), unresolved Python float
deterministic seeding: the same Generator seed gives bitwise-identical outputs (both backends); a different seed gives different outputs for a nondegenerate vector
L = 0: every molecule collected with zero hits and v_out identical to v0; K_back = 1
specular limits (Maxwell alpha = 0; CLL alpha_n = alpha_t = 0) with theta = 0 entry: f_trans = 1, f_back = 0, v_out_z identical to v0_z for every molecule, |v_out| = |v0| to 1e-9 relative

hit budget: an unresolved molecule has hits equal to the final budget; with max_hits = 2, max_hits_cap = 4 (E4-14) the final budget is 4 and the unresolved molecules are reported and never counted collected
exit direction: collected molecules have v_out_z > 0, backscattered molecules have v_out_z < 0
every diffuse sample satisfies v . normal > 0
v_out . normal >= 0 for every sample; alpha_n = alpha_t = 0 reproduces specular reflection v_in - 2 (v_in . n) n to 1e-9 relative
n = 0: empty outputs of the declared shapes and an unresolved fraction that is NaN in both backends (the reference takes the mean of an empty array)
every entry velocity has v_z > 0; output shape (n,3) float64
all final velocities of collected and backscattered molecules are finite

documented_divergence.statement: max_hits < 1: the reference never terminates (budget stays 0); the Rust backend refuses with ValueError instead. The Python backend of the wrapper passes the call through unchanged. Not part of the comparison set.

speedup_measurement.workload_W1: F0 workload tpmc_trace_channel exactly: atmosphere(200.0, 'mean'), mean molecular mass, IntakeGeometry(area 0.5, L/d 5, phi 0.85) -> R, L; numpy.random.default_rng(11); entry (n = 20000, theta 0) + trace_channel Maxwell alpha 0.8, T_w 350 K
speedup_measurement.workload_W2: response-point kernel composite: W1 plus clausing_transmission(n = 20000) on the same geometry (the TPMC part of one intake_response point)
speedup_measurement.statistic: median wall-clock and median process CPU per backend in one session on one machine; speed-up = median_python / median_rust; the F0 recorded python median is quoted for reference, not reused
speedup_measurement.backends_timed: python = abep_sim.intake_tpmc functions directly; rust = abep_sim.design.tpmc_backend with backend='rust' (wrapper overhead included)

copied_from_v1_unchanged.statement: these fields are the v1 values unchanged (same workloads, vectors, n, observables, seeds and tolerance |delta| <= 5 sqrt(se_py^2 + se_rust^2), aggregate bound 4.0, exact invariants); the pinned inputs were verified unchanged at registration

seed_reuse_rationale: v1 requires fresh campaign seeds for a v2 that changes a tolerance, observable, vector set, seed, sample size or decision rule, and a new scoring_master_seed after a NOT_ADMITTED verdict plus code fix. Neither applies: v2 changes none of those parameters and follows ADMITTED verdicts, so there is no seed selection to guard against; the only change is the pinned reference sha256. Keeping scoring_master_seed 20261001 makes v2 the identical-workload re-run of the v1 campaign against the changed reference (A9.14 S10.4) and the v2 numbers directly comparable with v1.
documented_divergence_status_note: DIV-01 (max_hits < 1) is closed on the reference side by A9.9 S2.5 MCC-05: the reference now refuses it too. The list is copied unchanged; inputs outside the comparison set remain outside it.

v1_cross_check.statement: with identical seeds, vectors and numpy, the stored Python-backend per-test numbers of v2 are expected to equal the v1 numbers bitwise (step-2 bit-identity claim), and the Rust-backend numbers likewise if the rebuilt extension reproduces the v1 stream. The report records, per kernel and backend, how many stored tests match v1 bitwise. A mismatch is reported and investigated; it never changes a v2 verdict, which is decided only by decision_rules on the v2 numbers.

meaning_of_v2_verdict: ADMITTED under v2 means the same as under v1: an optional, explicitly selected backend='rust' inside the tested parity domain; never the default, never silently substituted, never used for frozen data, goldens or score-bearing evidence (Python canonical, A9.14 S10.3). NOT_ADMITTED is final for v2: the tolerance is never widened.
